reason: Classification: PARTIAL. The immutable raw hashes to 68e9ad571f34795094ed9df13c150e429ec363c0c6ff7adcff36e74e7faeb58b, matching the assigned job; the canonical URL, nested raw_files value, path-qualified raw backlink, and source target state are correct; candidate.md exactly equals receipt.source_page; suggestions.json equals receipt.suggestions; all existing candidate wikilinks resolve; and all five retained excerpts byte-match their cited raw ranges. The candidate accurately preserves the one-level, maximum-active-10-node hierarchy; distinct customer and contract model; payer and statement pairings; separate child rating; bounded-period and same-issue-day consolidation conditions; standalone-statement visibility and downstream suppression; invoice origin identifiers; Stripe-only provider boundary; delayed parent commit-alert evaluation; truncated parent-spend-alert sentence; and invoice/commit embeddable-dashboard incompatibility. It also appropriately leaves relationship mutation, complete nested validation, endpoint response and error contracts, invoice finalization, correction, and consolidation failure recovery unspecified. Approval is nevertheless blocked by material evidence and concept-precision defects. The grounding set does not include relationship-at-contract-creation, the child parent/customer identifiers, selective contract-ID access, the self-paid-overage and co-active-contract conditions, or the contract/invoice/breakdown endpoint examples, even though the candidate and customer/commit updates assert those exact facts. The amount warning correctly identifies the dollar-labeled $10M versus amount 10000000 tension under the independently documented USD-cent convention, and the same issue is visible for the dollar-labeled $200K/amount 200000 and $500K/amount 500000 pairs; however, the raw never labels its later 5000000 and 2000000 schedules as $5M and $2M, so those two claims invent a denomination where the page supplies none. The retained excerpts also omit the numeric payloads corresponding to the $200K and $500K labels. The currency update's anchor, under ## API denomination, does not match the actual ## Fiat currencies and API denomination heading. The credits update omits the troubleshooting condition that parent and child contracts be active during the same period. The invoicing durable prose omits the Stripe-only hierarchy limit even though its reciprocal-link description claims it and the suggestion warning is not canonical concept content. The reporting update overgeneralizes the source's optional parent-facing UI warning about double-counting the standalone parent statement and consolidated invoice into a rule about all standalone parent and child statements in analyses. The alert update says there is no eventual-delivery guarantee, while this raw establishes an evaluation/trigger limitation and does not define webhook delivery; those concerns must remain separate. The source also does not state what happens to a child invoice that misses consolidation eligibility, so no separate-routing, downstream-send, retry, or recovery outcome may be inferred. No dedicated hierarchy concept is required because the existing customers-and-contracts concept already covers hierarchy inputs, and the selected six existing concept targets are otherwise the right one-authority-per-concern destinations; no company, comparison, index, or log suggestion is warranted in this campaign mode. Because the correction changes semantic cautions, concept content, and grounding across several sections, the unchanged-hash retry requires another full-source review.
required_changes: Narrow the amount contradiction to the pairs the raw actually dollar-labels: $10M with amount 10000000, $200K with amount 200000, and $500K with amount 500000. Remove the asserted $5M and $2M examples; the later 5000000 and 2000000 schedules have no dollar label, currency, or pricing-unit identifier, so their denomination is unknown. Add byte-exact grounding that contains both the $200K/$500K labels and their corresponding payload amounts, retain the USD-cent authority and no-undocumented-custom-unit warning, and change the currency suggestion anchor to the exact existing heading under ## Fiat currencies and API denomination.

Repair grounding coverage while retaining three to five byte-exact excerpts. The evidence used by hierarchical-customer-contract-model and hierarchical-commit-child-access must include relationship configuration during contract creation; child parent contract/customer identifiers plus payer and usage-statement fields; all, none, and contract_ids access; the self-paid-overage result; and the active-during-the-same-period troubleshooting condition. Add or expand evidence for the candidate's POST /v2/contracts/get, POST /v1/invoices/get, POST /v1/invoices/breakdown, constituent-invoice, origin-field, and grouping claims, then update every affected quote_indexes array.

Add the missing co-active parent/child contract condition to the shared-commit discussion and credits durable update. Preserve the existing lifecycle unknowns and explicitly avoid inventing the disposition of a child invoice that fails the bounded-service-period or same-issue-day checks: this page does not say whether it is routed separately, withheld from the provider, retried, surfaced as an error, or later consolidated. Do not infer enforcement or failure responses for cycles, duplicate parents, node-limit violations, reparenting, detachment, deletion, or concurrent hierarchy changes.

Carry the provider compatibility fact in canonical concept prose: update hierarchical-consolidated-invoicing, or an equally authoritative single concept target, to state that hierarchy billing currently supports only Stripe and that marketplace billing is merely described as coming soon without a date or provider contract. Do not leave this fact only in a suggestion warning or reciprocal-link description, and do not use the general Stripe integration source as independent proof of hierarchy support or of consolidation delivery and failure semantics.

Narrow hierarchical-reporting-origin-and-dashboard-limit to the raw's documented caution: Metronome suggests filtering the standalone parent usage statement in a parent-facing spend UI to avoid double-counting it with the consolidated invoice. Do not turn that into a blanket rule about all standalone parent and child statements or all analyses without exported-grain evidence. In hierarchical-parent-alert-limits, replace eventual-delivery language with evaluation/trigger language and keep webhook delivery mechanics separate; preserve that child-only usage may delay the parent alert until parent usage arrives, the page gives no latency or eventual-evaluation guarantee, the spend-alert sentence is truncated after parent spend alerts only include parent's, and the dashboard incompatibility is limited to invoice and commit embeddable dashboards for customers with a contract in a hierarchy.
